Compatibility.ai_packages_needed: fio (install) + a user-designated EMPTY test volume (NOT the OS disk; fio overwrites it)
Compatibility.ai_commands:
# fio mixed random read/write benchmark (DESTRUCTIVE I/O)
# FIO_TARGET must be a USER-DESIGNATED, EMPTY/clearable TEST VOLUME
#   e.g. an empty raw block device /dev/nvmeXn1, or an empty mount point /mnt/fiotest
# NEVER point it at the OS system disk (/, /boot) or any in-use volume - fio overwrites it.
FIO_TARGET="${FIO_TARGET:?set to a user-designated empty test volume (NOT the OS disk)}"
RUNTIME="${RUNTIME:-60}"    # seconds; confirm the sustained runtime first (item may say 43200s)
command -v fio >/dev/null 2>&1 || { apt-get update && apt-get install -y fio; }
cat > /tmp/fio-mix.fio <<EOF
[global]
ioengine=libaio
direct=1
group_reporting
randrepeat=0
refill_buffers
clocksource=clock_gettime
overwrite=1
ramp_time=10s
runtime=$RUNTIME
time_based
iodepth=1
numjobs=1
bs=512
rw=randrw
rwmixread=70

[test]
filename=$FIO_TARGET
EOF
fio /tmp/fio-mix.fio 2>&1 | tee /tmp/fio-mix.log
Compatibility.ai_logs_output: return /tmp/fio-mix.log (read IOPS, write IOPS, BW MB/s, latency) and confirm the result matches the SSD spec. Destructive sustained I/O on the designated target only - confirm runtime first.
Compatibility.risk: RISK: fio randrw/randwrite performs sustained destructive overwrite; run ONLY against a user-designated empty test volume and confirm the runtime first. NEVER target the OS system disk (/, /boot) or any in-use volume.

Reliability.Items: 1 Bank VLS then 2nd Strike to Buddy Rank, Region not in VLS
Reliability.Procedure:
【Before Test】
1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).
3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation
Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling
The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts:
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration >
	— EV DFX Features = Enable
	— Disable BIOS Done = [X]

ELOG Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Error Support= Enable
	— EMCA Logging Support= Enable
	— Corrected Error eLog = Enable
	— Memory Error eLog = Enable
	— Processor Error eLog = Enable

Error Reporting Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings >
	— WHEA Support = Enable
	— WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable
	— WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable

Error Injection Enabling
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log >
	— System Errors = Enable
	— System Memory Poison = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings >
	— MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable
	— WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling >
	— IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable
	— IIO MCA Support = Disable
	— IIO eDPC Support = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable

Firmware First Model
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings >
	— EMCA Logging Support = Enable
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI
	— EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0
	— EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable

Crash Log
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable

4. Other OS Notes
You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable".

【During Test】
1. Specific BIOS setup :
• EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling >
	— Spare Interrupt = SMI
• EDKII > Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration >
	— Correctable Error Threshold = 2
	— Trigger SW Error Threshold= Disabled
	— ADDDC Sparing = Enable
• Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration >
	— Enforce Population POR = Disable
• Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used to create this recipe. It is recommended to have a POR memory population.

2. Establish 1 bank VLS region as described in One Bank VLS Region.

3. Halt the system for error injections.
>>> halt()

4. The hardware per rank CECC error thresholds were set to "2" so inject two CECC errors to the buddy rank and bank. In step 1, a bank VLS region was established
with the buddy rank as chip-select 0x4 and bank 0x1. Chip-select decodes to {DIMM, rank, sub-channel}. Use these DIMM, rank, and sub-channel values as the new error injection target BUT use a bank other than 0x1.
>>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=0, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0)
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=1, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False)
>>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=0, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=1, dev1msk=0x0)
>>> ei.mem.injectMemError(socket=0, channel=0, dimm=1, rank=0, sub_channel=0, bank_group=0, bank=0, errType="ce", verbose=True, sub_rank=0, ps_ch=0, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False)

5. Check that the per rank CECC error threshold has been met.
>>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0)

6. Resume the system so BIOS can perform its SMM flow.
>>> go()

7. Expecting bank VLS sparing to occur so copy_in_progress should be 1.
>>> sv.socket0.compute0.uncore.memss.mc0.ch0.mcchan.sparing_patrol_status.show()

8. Verify that the initial bank VLS region remains the same, the per rank CECC error counter was cleared, and the 2nd bank VLS region was established.
>>> ras.mem.adddc_status_check(socket=0, mc=0)

Error is injected successfully.
Error logs should match.
